overlay.title: Meeting prompter
overlay.clearEarlierTitle: Hide the earlier questions from this list. They stay in this meeting, and Restore brings them back.
overlay.emptyBody: When someone asks you something, hints appear here.
overlay.latencyMedian: Median {{value}} s · open the latency probe
overlay.latencyBreakdown: Last hint {{total}} s: recognition {{asr}} · detection {{detect}} · hints {{generate}}
overlay.probeAgain: Hints have been slow for several questions. Run the latency probe again?
overlay.askTitle: Type a question the recognizer missed or got wrong
overlay.longerTitle: Write the hints again with more specifics and an example
overlay.againTitle: Write a fresh set of hints from another angle
overlay.recognitionDownHint: MeetCue keeps reconnecting, but no new hints come until it's back. Answer from your own notes for now.
overlay.hintsDownHint: The last hint requests didn't finish. Check the connection to your model provider, or answer from your own notes for now.

settings.title: Settings
settings.uiLanguageHint: Changes apply immediately in every window.
settings.hintLanguageHint: Language of the talking points and the sample answer.
settings.autostart: Start MeetCue when I sign in
settings.hideInShare: Hide the panel when sharing the screen
settings.hideInShareHint: Screen sharing and most recorders won't capture the panel. Some recording methods and capture hardware still can.
settings.clickThrough: Let clicks pass through the panel
settings.clickThroughHint: The panel fades and stops catching the mouse, so you can click what is behind it. Turn it off with the shortcut or from the tray icon.
settings.panelLayoutHint: Also switches with {{key}} and the buttons on the panel.
settings.panelPositionHint: Drag the panel from any empty spot to move it, or use Move on the panel to snap it to an edge or a saved spot. This puts it back at the top right of the main screen.
settings.setupAgainHint: Walk through languages, audio, models, keys and the latency check again. Your current settings are kept as the starting point.
settings.helpDocsHint: Guides, shortcuts and fixes for common problems. Problems with a meeting? The activity log and diagnostics export are under Diagnostics.
settings.practiceOpenHint: Questions are read aloud and you answer over your microphone, with hints and a review. Sample interviews are included.
settings.fontHint: Used in the panel and every window. The sample beside the list shows how it looks.
settings.panelTextHint: Larger text is easier to read at a glance; smaller text fits more in a short panel.
settings.panelOpacityHint: A see-through panel lets you keep an eye on what is behind it.
settings.panelSizeHint: Width and height of the panel. You can also drag its edges; the size you set is kept.
settings.spotsHint: Put the panel where it hides nothing, then save the spot here or from Move on the panel. Its shortcut brings the panel back there, with the same size and layout.
settings.hintActionsHint: Shows Shorter, More detail and Another take under a question's hints, and an Ask button to type a question the recognizer missed. Each use is one hint request.
settings.connectionAlerts: Tell me when recognition or hints stop working
settings.connectionAlertsHint: Shows a notice on the panel when speech recognition stays disconnected for 10 seconds or hint requests fail twice in a row.

audio.bluetoothWarning: Using a Bluetooth headset microphone lowers playback quality for the whole call. Use the built-in microphone instead if you can.
audio.remoteHint: MeetCue listens to everything played through the default output device.
audio.levelsHint: Play some audio and speak: both bars should move.
audio.boostQuiet: Boost quiet voices from the meeting
audio.boostQuietHint: Raises soft-spoken participants to a normal speaking level before recognition, so their questions are caught. Your own microphone is not changed.
audio.remoteThresholdHint: Sound from the meeting quieter than this is not sent for recognition. Lower it if soft-spoken participants are missed; raise it if music or noise in the meeting is transcribed.
audio.vadHint: Lower picks up quieter speech from you; higher ignores more background noise in your room.
audio.endpointHint: How long a pause ends a sentence. Shorter shows hints sooner but may split a question in two; longer waits through pauses in long questions.
audio.languagesHint: Main language first. Soniox recognises Chinese and English mixed in one sentence; Deepgram recognises only the main language.
audio.deepgramMixed: Deepgram can't recognise Chinese and English in the same stream, so it will only recognise {{language}}. For mixed speech, choose Soniox in Providers & cost.
audio.appliesLive: These settings, the microphone and the languages apply immediately, also during a meeting.
audio.speakerLabelsHint: Asks the speech recognizer who said each sentence and shows "Speaker 2" on the question card. Works with Soniox and Deepgram. Deepgram charges extra for it; Soniox doesn't.

providers.asrLead: Turns both sides of the call into text. Billed by audio time.
providers.detectLead: Spots questions meant for you. A cheap, fast model is enough.
providers.hintsLead: Writes the talking points. Faster models show hints sooner.
providers.estimateFormula: Speech recognition: price × 2 channels × share of time with speech. Models: questions per hour × (detection + hint call), with the system prompt at the cache-read price, plus 10% for cancelled early triggers.
providers.endpointHint: Auto uses the fastest endpoint from your last latency probe.
providers.keysLead: Set a base URL to use a gateway, proxy or self-hosted server. Keys stay in your system's credential store, never in settings files or logs.
providers.assumptionsLead: The hourly estimates use these numbers. Change them to match your meetings.
providers.proxyHint: Leave empty to use the system proxy settings.
providers.systemTokensHint: The hint instructions, your role and the knowledge base excerpt, billed at the cache-read price.
providers.cancelOverheadHint: Extra share for requests started early and then cancelled.
providers.ownPricesLead: To track spending against your budget, enter the price for models without a listed price, or to replace a listed one.
providers.keysNone: Choose a provider above to enter its address and key.
providers.modelsLead: Choose a provider, then pick a model from the list or type any name it offers. The list shows each model's price and the estimated cost of a meeting hour; once a key is saved, it adds every model your account offers.

probe.title: Latency probe
probe.lead: Measures how fast each provider responds from your network, so you can choose with real numbers.
probe.label: Network label
probe.costBody: The probe sends about 30 seconds of audio to each speech service and makes about 8 short model calls. That usually costs a few cents in total.
probe.noKeys: No API keys yet, so only network timing (DNS, connection and TLS) is measured.
probe.legend: Median / slowest, in milliseconds. Speech: start of speech to first partial, and end of audio to final text. Models: request to first token, and to the first complete talking point.
probe.estimateNote: Estimated delay = sentence-end wait + recognition + detection + first talking point.

budget.title: Budget
budget.lead: Get a warning at 80% and choose what happens at 100%. Leave empty for no limit.

usage.title: Usage {{month}}
usage.lead: Usage reported by the providers, converted with the price table.
usage.cachedHint: Share of input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache, which are billed at a fraction of the price and read faster.
usage.estimateNote: Estimates. Your provider's bill is authoritative.
usage.unpricedHint: Some calls have no price in the list, so the real cost is higher.

hints.roleHint: Helps the hints match how you would answer.
hints.rolePlaceholder: e.g. Network architect with 8 years in data center operations
hints.onlyDirectedToMeHint: Skip questions that are clearly meant for someone else.
hints.queueInterruptionsHint: A question asked while you are answering waits as the next question instead of replacing the current one.
hints.trackCoverage: Tick off points as I speak
hints.trackCoverageHint: Listens to your microphone while you answer, ticks the points you have said and highlights the next one. It can tick or miss points when your wording differs from the list. When off, click a point to tick it yourself.
hints.earlyTriggerHint: Start as soon as a question looks finished instead of waiting for the end of the sentence. Faster, but occasionally redone.
hints.speculativeHints: Write hints while checking the question
hints.speculativeHintsHint: Starts the hints at the same time as the check whether a sentence is a question, instead of after it. About a second faster; a sentence that turns out not to be a question costs one unused hint request.
hints.meetingMemoryHint: Gives the hint model one line per earlier question with what you answered, for the whole meeting, so follow-ups stay consistent after the recent transcript has moved on. Adds a few hundred words to hint requests late in a long meeting.
hints.skipRepeatedSentencesHint: A sentence that repeats one checked in the last two minutes, such as a question asked again, isn't sent to the detection model a second time. Saves detection requests.

shortcuts.lead: Shortcuts work while other apps have focus.
shortcuts.moveLead: Keep the panel right under your camera so your eyes don't wander while you read. Tap to move a little, hold to keep moving.
shortcuts.why: The defaults avoid common shortcuts of meeting apps, input methods and graphics drivers.
shortcuts.spotsTitle: Panel spots and getting it out of the way
shortcuts.spotsLead: Pressing a spot shortcut moves the panel to that saved spot. On an empty spot it saves where the panel is now.
shortcuts.peek: Hide the panel for a few seconds
shortcuts.clickThrough: Let clicks pass through the panel (on/off)

diag.exportLead: Creates a zip file you can attach to a bug report. API keys and tokens are removed, and transcripts, knowledge base files and custom prompts are not included.
diag.debugLoggingHint: Also writes full transcripts to the log. Turn off after troubleshooting.
diag.logLead: What MeetCue is doing right now: starting and pausing, audio arriving, sentences recognised, questions and errors. Transcripts appear only with debug logging on.

wizard.title: Set up MeetCue
wizard.lead: A few steps and you're ready for your next meeting.
wizard.languageLead: Choose the interface language. You can change it any time.
wizard.audioLead: MeetCue listens to your microphone and to what the other participants say through your speakers or headphones.
wizard.modelsLead: Choose a provider and type any model name it offers for each task, then enter the address and key. You can change them later in Settings.
wizard.chooseAll: Choose a model for each of the three tasks to continue.
wizard.keysMissing: Some keys are missing. You can add them later in Settings.
wizard.doneBody: Press {{key}} when the meeting starts. The panel stays on top without taking focus.
wizard.doneDemo: Want to see it first? Start MeetCue with --demo to replay a sample interview without keys.
wizard.donePractice: No meeting handy? A mock interview reads questions aloud and shows hints exactly as in a meeting, so you can test everything on your own.
wizard.tryPractice: Finish and try a mock interview

gallery.title: MeetCue preview
gallery.lead: This browser preview replays a recorded sample interview through the real interface. No microphone or API keys are used.

practice.title: Mock interview
practice.lead: Rehearse an interview on your own, without a real meeting. Questions are read aloud, hints appear in the panel exactly as in a meeting, and you get a review at the end.
practice.importHint: Subtitles (.srt, .vtt, .txt) or a question list (.txt, .md, .csv). Files are read on this computer; only text goes to the model.
practice.question: Question
practice.meSpeakerHint: Your lines aren't read aloud; they become the reference answers in the review.
practice.classifyBody: The hint model can label each line as a question or an answer. Check the result before you start.
practice.simulatedNote: Only recognition delay is simulated; the model's delay is real.
practice.levelHint: Step down one level at a time until you can answer without hints.
practice.followUpsHint: Sometimes asks one short follow-up about your answer.
practice.recognizeMeHint: Needed for ticks and most review figures. When off, your answers cause no recognition cost.
practice.stopOnSpeech: Stop reading when I start speaking
practice.runningBody: Hints appear in the panel. Answer aloud; a pause of {{seconds}} seconds ends your answer.

phase.nudge: Take your time. Start when you're ready.

practice.finishedBody: The review opens in its own window.
practice.hintsOff: Hints are hidden at this level. You'll see them in the review.
practice.fillersHint: Counted in the review. Separate words with commas.
practice.howBriefing: Optional: add the matching job description to your knowledge base, so hints fit the role.
practice.samplesLead: Built into MeetCue, with reference answers for the review: two in English, two in Chinese. Each asks one question at a time, and you can trim and reorder the list before you start.

sweQuestions.title: Software engineer
sweQuestions.body: 14 questions on fundamentals, algorithms, system design, debugging and teamwork.

securityQuestions.title: Network security and AI
securityQuestions.body: 12 questions on TLS, zero trust, detection, incident response, ML for security and LLM security.

sweQuestionsZh.title: Backend software engineer (Chinese)
sweQuestionsZh.body: 14 questions on networking, databases, caching, system design, troubleshooting and teamwork.

networkOpsZh.title: Telecom network operations (Chinese)
networkOpsZh.body: 42 scenario questions on major incidents, home broadband, IP and enterprise lines, optical transport, 5G, data centers and management.

practice.sttQuestionsOn: On, like a real meeting: each question is spoken aloud, captured from system sound and transcribed by your speech provider, so you get the same delay as in a meeting. Use headphones.
practice.sttQuestionsOff: Off: each question is still spoken aloud, but its text goes straight to the hint model after a recognition delay taken from your last latency probe. Saves recognition cost.
practice.soundLead: A mock interview works exactly like a meeting: the questions are spoken aloud and come back in through system sound, and your answers come in through the microphone.
practice.headphones: Put headphones on. With speakers, your microphone hears the questions too and may tick off talking points before you say a word.
practice.micHint: Say something. This bar should move.
practice.systemHint: Play a video or press Try it below. This bar should move.
practice.audioSettings: Both bars flat, or the wrong device?
practice.voiceTitle: The voice that asks the questions
practice.voiceLead: Questions are read by a system voice. Pick one per language and listen to it before you start.
practice.voiceHint: Add voices in your system speech settings. On macOS: Accessibility › Spoken Content (Read & Speak on newer versions). On Windows: Time & language › Speech.
practice.noVoices: No system speech voices are available. Add a voice in your system speech settings, then reopen this window.
practice.nextCheck: Next: check the questions, then start.
practice.nextStart: When you press Start, the first question is read aloud. Answer out loud; a pause of {{seconds}} seconds ends your answer.

next.speaking: Listen; hints appear when the question ends. Start talking at any time to interrupt.
next.waiting: Your turn. Answer out loud; a pause of {{seconds}} seconds ends your answer.
next.answering: Keep going. Points tick off as you cover them; a pause of {{seconds}} seconds ends your answer.
next.followUp: Writing a follow-up question about your answer.
next.paused: Paused. Nothing is sent to any provider.
next.done: Finished. The review opens in its own window.

practice.selectTip: Tick rows to change several at once. Shift-click a second row to tick everything in between.
practice.addQuestionHint: Type a question of your own
practice.jumpLead: Jump forwards or back at any time. The current answer is kept; a question you leave unanswered counts as skipped.

missingVoice.en: No English voice is installed, so English questions can't be read aloud.
missingVoice.zh: No Chinese voice is installed, so Chinese questions can't be read aloud.

missingVoiceSteps.en: In Windows Settings › Time & language › Language & region, add English (United States) and tick Text-to-speech, or open Speech and choose Add voices. Then reopen this window. On macOS, open System Settings › Accessibility › Spoken Content (or Read & Speak), choose Manage Voices and download a voice for this language.
missingVoiceSteps.zh: In Windows Settings › Time & language › Language & region, add Chinese (Simplified, China) and tick Text-to-speech, or open Speech and choose Add voices. Then reopen this window. On macOS, open System Settings › Accessibility › Spoken Content (or Read & Speak), choose Manage Voices and download a voice for this language.

practice.generateLead: Uses your role and knowledge base files (Settings › Hints), such as a job description and your résumé, to write the questions an interviewer is likely to ask, with reference answers. One request to your hint model.
practice.generateNeedsMaterial: Add your role or a job description in Settings › Hints first.

review.title: Practice review
review.simulatedNote: Recognition delay was simulated; model latency is real.
review.noTranscript: No transcript: recognition was off or nothing was heard.
review.trendLead: Time to start and coverage across your practice sessions.

tray.clickThrough: Let clicks pass through the panel

wipe.title: Erase all data
wipe.label: Start over
wipe.hint: Removes your API keys from the system credential store and deletes everything MeetCue saved on this computer, then restarts MeetCue as if newly installed. Use it before handing the computer to someone else or uninstalling.
wipe.itemKeys: All API keys saved in the system credential store
wipe.itemSettings: Your settings, including materials and shortcuts
wipe.itemRecords: Practice reports, usage and cost records, and latency check history
wipe.confirmLead: It can't be undone. Export anything you want to keep first.
wipe.failed: Some data could not be erased: {{detail}}

latencyTips.speculative: Turn on “Write hints while checking the question” in Settings › Hints. It saves one model round trip, usually about a second.
latencyTips.earlyTrigger: Most of the time goes into waiting for the sentence to end. Turn on “Start hints early” in Settings › Hints.
latencyTips.endpoint: Most of the time goes into waiting for the sentence to end. Lower “Sentence end after silence” (now {{value}} s) in Settings › Audio › Advanced.
latencyTips.detectModel: The question check is the slow part. Pick a small, fast model for detection in Settings › Providers & cost: it only answers yes or no.
latencyTips.hintModel: Writing the hints is the slow part. Pick a faster hint model in Settings › Providers & cost, or keep the knowledge base short.
latencyTips.network: No single stage stands out. Run the latency probe to find the fastest providers and endpoints from this network, and turn off a VPN if you use one.

placement.title: Move and size the panel
placement.drag: Drag anywhere on the panel to move it
placement.snap: Snap to an edge or corner
placement.spotsLead: Save a spot for each layout you use, such as one beside the shared screen and one under the camera.
placement.seeThrough: See and reach what is behind it
placement.peekHint: To click something behind the panel. Comes back on its own.
placement.throughHint: The panel fades and ignores the mouse. To undo, press
placement.throughOn: Clicks pass through the panel. Press {{key}} or use the tray icon to stop.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.lead: Your résumé, project notes, slides or job description, so hints use your real experience instead of generic answers. Text is extracted on this computer.
knowledge.filesHint: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, RTF, HTML, text and Markdown. Old .doc, .xls and .ppt files need to be saved in the newer format first.
knowledge.modeWhole: Short enough to send with every question.
knowledge.modeSearch: Each question gets the passages that match it, plus a short overview of every file.
knowledge.tryHint: See which passages the hint model would get for a question. Nothing is sent anywhere.
knowledge.tryPlaceholder: e.g. Tell me about a time you handled an outage
knowledge.allSent: Your files are short, so all of them go with every question.
knowledge.noMatch: No passage matches this question. The hints still get the overview below.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.lead: The instructions MeetCue gives the hint model. Change them to adjust tone, length or focus. Keep the reply format (numbered JSON lines, then ---, then the sample answer), or the panel can't show the hints.
prompts.hintsSystemHint: Same for every question, so providers can cache it. Placeholders: {{placeholders}}
prompts.hintsUserHint: Sent with each question; {knowledge} becomes the matching knowledge base passages. Placeholders: {{placeholders}}
prompts.missing: Missing {{placeholders}}: that information won't reach the model.

models.loading: Loading the models on your {{provider}} account…
models.needsKey: Showing models with listed prices. Save a {{provider}} key below to see every model your account offers.
models.footAsr: Per meeting hour: both sides of the call for the share of time with speech. Prices are from the provider's pricing page.
models.footLlm: Per meeting hour: detection or hint calls for the questions in an hour. Prices are from the provider's pricing page.
models.noPriceChosen: No listed price for this model. Add one under Your own prices to track spending.
models.empty: No models to show. Type the name of any {{provider}} model.

ask.title: Type a question
ask.placeholder: e.g. How would you design a rate limiter?
ask.hint: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line.

meetings.title: Meeting
meetings.lead: After you stop listening, MeetCue keeps a recap of the meeting on this computer: the questions, the hints you saw and which points you ticked. Nothing is sent anywhere.
meetings.save: Save a recap of each meeting
meetings.saveHint: Free: the recap is built from what the panel showed, without extra model calls.
meetings.saveTranscript: Also save everything that was said
meetings.saveTranscriptHint: Keeps the full transcript of both sides with the recap. Off by default; only turn it on where recording a meeting is allowed.
meetings.keepHint: Older meetings are deleted when a new one is saved.
meetings.empty: No meetings saved yet. They appear here after you stop listening.
meetings.missing: This meeting is no longer saved.
meetings.noQuestions: No questions were detected in this meeting.
